tasks.short: Recommend technologies against actual database performance needs

steps.what: Check the desired database performance, current bottlenecks and operating constraints
inputs: operations-maintained dated workload and bottleneck observations
application-owner performance targets and constraints
outputs: checked technology evaluation requirements

steps.what: Identify candidate hardware or software technologies from the approved technology catalogue and available technical documentation
inputs: checked technology evaluation requirements
technology-owner catalogue with capabilities, support status and technical-document versions
outputs: candidate technology evidence table and missing evidence

steps.what: Evaluate candidate technologies for database performance fit, integration, operability and limitations
inputs: candidate technology evidence table and missing evidence
checked technology evaluation requirements
outputs: architect-written suitability assessments and explicit quantitative assumptions

steps.what: Calculate comparable capacity and cost scenarios from the explicit evaluation assumptions
inputs: architect-written suitability assessments and explicit quantitative assumptions
candidate technology evidence table and missing evidence
outputs: checked quantitative comparison with assumption sensitivities

steps.what: Write the technology recommendation, conditions and evidence gaps for the named internal decision owner
inputs: architect-written suitability assessments and explicit quantitative assumptions
checked quantitative comparison with assumption sensitivities
outputs: complete recommendation with exact internal recipient

steps.what: Check and approve the final recommendation and recipient
inputs: complete recommendation with exact internal recipient
outputs: approved technology recommendation packet v1

steps.what: Save the approved recommendation in its existing internal architecture record
inputs: approved technology recommendation packet v1
outputs: stored technology recommendation

steps.what: Send the approved recommendation to the named internal decision owner
inputs: approved technology recommendation packet v1
stored technology recommendation
outputs: delivered technology recommendation

tasks.design: Configure workload views in the {DATA_PLATFORM}, candidate filters in the {DOCS} catalogue and comparison formulas in the {SPREADSHEET}. The architect evaluates suitability and writes a qualified recommendation, then approves its final version and recipient before storage and delivery.
tasks.previous_blocker: Known technology evidence and repeatable scenario calculations can require repeated navigation and reconstruction.
tasks.enabler_now: Native catalogue filters and checked formulas can reuse explicit evidence without ranking technologies as a substitute for judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Published capability or an estimated capacity is not proof of performance in this workload.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when an attractive option cannot satisfy operational constraints or lacks credible evidence.

ambition.what: Re-evaluate the preferred capacity option when a material workload assumption changes.

reach.task: Frame technology evaluation criteria before purchasing
reach.learn: Separate technical requirements from commercial terms and supplier claims.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-4 for workload, catalogue and cost access

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: metadata filters and explicit scenario formulas can support technology comparison without deciding suitability.

assumptions: Boundary is identification, evaluation and recommendation, not purchase or deployment. Recommendation delivery remains a separate gated action.

Operations supplies workload metric, period, units and query class; application owners supply targets. Technology owners supply candidate id, document version and stated capability. Missing evidence is manually sought in s1/s2 or marked absent; no free research or extraction is assumed.
s3 captures scenario inputs and their units before s4 calculates. Native configuration first. If no structured catalogue exists, s2 remains manual and this scenario's saving falls.
All shares and reductions are provisional, not measured baselines. Same-system save and short internal send remain fully retained. No supplier or runtime labour is counted.
unknowns: Catalogue completeness and actual bottleneck data
research_questions: Can each candidate claim be traced to the supplied technical-document version?
Do sensitivity changes reverse the recommendation?

already_counted.description: Verify comparable scenario formulas, units and assumptions

approvals.approved_version: approved technology recommendation packet v1; edits void approval
approved technology recommendation packet v1 including recipient; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross 17.7 minus 1 upkeep gives 16.7. High allows 3.7 extra hours resolving incomplete candidate evidence; low covers already configured views or manual research dominating the work.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Test databases, diagnose errors and verify bounded corrections

steps.what: Define the program or database error, expected behaviour and isolated test boundary
inputs: reported error with reproduction evidence
application-owner behaviour requirements
operations-approved isolated environment and data restrictions
outputs: architect-written test specification and permitted sandbox scope

steps.what: Write the test cases and fixture setup needed to reproduce the error
inputs: architect-written test specification and permitted sandbox scope
existing permitted test harness and synthetic fixtures
outputs: complete draft test execution packet v1

loop.input: Human-written expected behaviour, permitted harness and synthetic fixture schema
loop.output: Candidate test cases and fixture setup limited to the approved isolated environment
loop.check: Architect checks assertions against intended meaning, negative cases, fixture safety and permitted scope; passing syntax alone is insufficient
loop.stop: Stop after two rejected drafts or any unclear expected result and write the test manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Existing harness configuration comes first; new error-specific assertions require interpreting the specification

steps.what: Review and approve the exact reproduction tests, fixture setup and sandbox target
inputs: complete draft test execution packet v1
outputs: approved reproduction execution packet v1

steps.what: Set up and execute the approved reproduction tests in the isolated database environment
inputs: approved reproduction execution packet v1
outputs: actual reproduction test results and execution log

steps.what: Diagnose the program or database errors from the actual results and specify necessary modifications
inputs: actual reproduction test results and execution log
architect-written test specification and permitted sandbox scope
outputs: architect-authored correction intent and invariants

steps.what: Code the necessary program or database modification and its regression cases
inputs: architect-authored correction intent and invariants
actual reproduction test results and execution log
current program or database definition snapshot
outputs: complete candidate correction and regression execution packet v2

loop.purpose: Draft an error-specific correction and regression cases
loop.input: Current definition, human diagnosis, correction intent and invariants
loop.output: Bounded candidate diff and regression cases, with no execution permission
loop.check: Architect reviews semantic behaviour, data-loss risk, transaction boundaries, negative cases and unchanged invariants against the diagnosis
loop.stop: Stop after two unsuccessful drafts or any unclear destructive effect; correct manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Use an existing known fix first; a novel code correction requires interpreting intended behaviour

steps.what: Approve the exact candidate correction and regression tests for isolated execution
inputs: complete candidate correction and regression execution packet v2
outputs: approved isolated regression packet v2

steps.what: Execute the approved correction and regression tests only in the approved isolated environment
inputs: approved isolated regression packet v2
outputs: actual corrected-run results and execution log

steps.what: Verify actual regression results and complete the final correction and test evidence record
inputs: actual corrected-run results and execution log
approved isolated regression packet v2
architect-authored correction intent and invariants
outputs: complete correction record v3 with exact diff and actual test evidence

steps.what: Approve the exact final verified correction and evidence record
inputs: complete correction record v3 with exact diff and actual test evidence
outputs: approved correction record v3 with exact diff and actual test evidence

steps.what: Save the approved correction and test evidence in the existing development record
inputs: approved correction record v3 with exact diff and actual test evidence
outputs: stored verified correction record

tasks.design: Use the existing {DATA_PLATFORM} test harness and bounded drafting assistance for error-specific tests and corrections held in the {DOCS}. The architect defines expected behaviour, approves each complete sandbox execution packet, diagnoses actual results and approves the verified correction record; production deployment is a separate workflow.
tasks.previous_blocker: New reproduction cases and small corrections require bespoke code, but broad autonomous execution would exceed the intended authority.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded draft-and-review loop can work inside an existing test harness while execution remains explicitly gated.
tasks.still_hard: A passing regression suite can still encode the wrong expectation or miss data-loss behaviour.
tasks.human_edge: Diagnose causality, select meaningful assertions and reject superficially passing fixes.

ambition.what: Offer a reproducible defect evidence pack with each database correction.

reach.task: Design regression cases for database changes
reach.learn: Failure isolation, negative assertions and fixture design.

build_days.consent_and_access: 2-6 for isolated execution access and permitted test data; consult owners on data use

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: bounded code drafting can propose tests and corrections, while existing test runners execute an explicitly approved packet.

assumptions: Boundary is testing and correcting in an existing isolated development environment and recording the verified change. Production deployment is separately authorised; no production benefit or other-role saving is counted.

Error reporter supplies reproduction evidence; application owners supply expected behaviour; operations supplies an already isolated environment and permitted synthetic fixtures. Missing specifications and fixture adjustments remain in s1/s2/s4, not free inputs.

Test native harness configuration and known corrections before a model loop. The loop cannot execute tools. A changed test, diff, fixture or target invalidates its execution approval; failed results return to diagnosis and renewed review.

Shares and retained percentages are provisional scenarios, not measured baselines. s4/s8 reductions concern repeated human setup and command assembly, never machine runtime or waiting. Their remaining time counts setup checks and run inspection.
Final saving is fully retained as an approximately zero-effort same-system action. No automatic notifications or production commits are hidden in the design.
unknowns: Existing harness coverage and isolation controls
Amount of bespoke versus known correction work
research_questions: Can an architect detect an intentionally wrong assertion in a proposed reproduction case?
Do actual setup savings exceed the extra code review and upkeep?

already_counted.description: Inspect drafted test semantics and fixtures
Inspect drafted correction behaviour and regression cases

incremental.description: Maintain prompt boundaries, harness integration and regression checks for drafting assistance

approvals.approved_version: approved reproduction execution packet v1 including fixtures and isolated target; changes void approval
approved isolated regression packet v2 including exact correction, tests, fixtures and target; changes void approval
approved correction record v3 with exact diff and actual test evidence; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross 17.4 minus 2 upkeep gives 15.4. High allows 4.4 more hours reviewing novel faults; low is no drafting/setup gain with two hours of upkeep still incurred.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Identify and correct database development standard deviations

steps.what: Compare database definitions with the current development standards to identify deviations
inputs: current definition snapshot
standard-owner versioned machine-checkable rules and written semantic standards
outputs: checked deviation candidates with rule and object references

steps.what: Determine which deviations are genuine and specify corrections or justified exceptions
inputs: checked deviation candidates with rule and object references
standard-owner versioned machine-checkable rules and written semantic standards
outputs: architect-written correction instructions and exception reasons

steps.what: Write corrected database definitions for the confirmed deviations
inputs: architect-written correction instructions and exception reasons
current definition snapshot
outputs: complete candidate definition diff

loop.purpose: Draft a correction for semantic standards deviations
loop.input: Exact definition snapshot, human-confirmed deviation and correction instruction
loop.output: Candidate definition diff with per-change standard references
loop.check: Architect checks intended data meaning, compatibility, affected references and absence of unauthorised changes, not just rule compliance
loop.stop: Stop after two rejected drafts, uncertain compatibility or any destructive change and correct manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Native lint fixes come first; remaining semantic deviations need interpretation of the human correction instruction

steps.what: Run non-mutating definition and standards checks on the candidate diff and inspect the results
inputs: complete candidate definition diff
standard-owner versioned machine-checkable rules and written semantic standards
outputs: actual static-check results for the candidate version

steps.what: Review semantic compatibility and actual check results and approve the exact final definition correction
inputs: complete candidate definition diff
actual static-check results for the candidate version
architect-written correction instructions and exception reasons
outputs: approved definition correction v1

steps.what: Commit the approved definition correction to the existing internal development record without deploying it
inputs: approved definition correction v1
outputs: stored corrected definition version

steps.what: Record the actual corrected version, standards disposition and unresolved exceptions
inputs: stored corrected definition version
actual static-check results for the candidate version
architect-written correction instructions and exception reasons
outputs: complete standards disposition record

steps.what: Approve the final standards disposition record
inputs: complete standards disposition record
outputs: approved standards disposition v1

steps.what: Save the approved disposition in its existing internal standards record
inputs: approved standards disposition v1
outputs: stored standards disposition

tasks.design: Configure native standards checks against definitions in the {DATA_PLATFORM}, then use a bounded drafting loop only for confirmed deviations that native fixes cannot address. The architect judges compatibility, approves a checked correction in the {DOCS} and separately records its actual disposition in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Standards include both mechanical naming rules and semantic requirements that a linter cannot decide.
tasks.enabler_now: Native linting removes repeated mechanical inspection; a constrained draft can implement a human-specified semantic correction without receiving execution rights.
tasks.still_hard: A standards-compliant change can break application assumptions or require an exception.
tasks.human_edge: Decide whether a deviation is intentional and whether correction is safer than retaining it.

ambition.what: Review standards exceptions when an affected interface changes rather than waiting for a broad audit.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-5 for definition access and authorised standards ownership

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: static database checks can find declared-rule deviations; bounded drafting can propose changes that still need compatibility review.

assumptions: Boundary includes identifying, coding and recording corrections in development definitions. Deployment remains separate; no runtime database is changed here. Overlap with generic error correction must be reconciled in roll-up.

Standard owners already supply rule id, version, applicability and severity; source owners supply an exact definition snapshot. Where rules are prose-only, manual interpretation stays in s1/s2 and no free rule extraction is assumed.

The architect creates correction instructions in s2; s3 cannot invent an approved exception. Native lint and known fixes first. s4 is non-mutating static analysis and needs no execution permission to write data.

All shares and reductions are provisional scenarios, not observed baselines. s1/s4 saving concerns human inspection and command setup, not machine runtime. Same-system commit and save remain fully retained.
s5 approval covers an already complete diff; any edit or changed source snapshot returns to checking and approval. The disposition is written after the actual correction is stored.
unknowns: Proportion of standards that are machine-checkable
Rate of semantic exceptions and compatibility impacts
research_questions: Can reviewers trace each proposed change to a confirmed deviation?
Do static checks miss any semantic break in a seeded correction?

incremental.description: Maintain standards rules, native checks and drafting constraints

approved standards disposition v1; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross 23.5 minus 1.5 upkeep gives 22. High allows five more hours for compatibility exceptions; low assumes no inspection or drafting gain but upkeep remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Code logical and physical database descriptions and identifiers

steps.what: Check the approved data model, target database management system and identifier conventions
inputs: approved model version and target dialect supplied by design owner
database-owner identifier and namespace conventions
outputs: checked coding requirements and model gaps

steps.what: Write logical and physical database descriptions and explicitly specify database identifiers, types, keys and constraints
inputs: checked coding requirements and model gaps
outputs: architect-authored complete logical and physical model with target identifiers

steps.what: Code the target database management system descriptions from the explicit model and identifier definitions
inputs: architect-authored complete logical and physical model with target identifiers
checked coding requirements and model gaps
outputs: complete draft target-dialect database description code

steps.what: Check coded descriptions against logical meaning, physical definitions, identifiers and namespace collisions
inputs: complete draft target-dialect database description code
architect-authored complete logical and physical model with target identifiers
database-owner identifier and namespace conventions
outputs: complete checked database description code

steps.what: Approve the exact final coded database descriptions for the development record
inputs: complete checked database description code
outputs: approved database description code v1

steps.what: Save the approved coded database descriptions in their existing internal development record
inputs: approved database description code v1
outputs: stored logical and physical database description code

tasks.design: Configure the {OTHER} database modelling tool to export target-dialect definitions from explicit logical and physical model fields. The architect specifies identifiers, checks generated code against meaning and namespace conventions, and approves the final version before saving it in the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Typing dialect-specific definitions can duplicate fields and identifiers already chosen in the model.
tasks.enabler_now: Native schema export can deterministically translate declared model attributes into supported code constructs.
tasks.still_hard: The model must express the right meaning, and unsupported dialect features need manual treatment.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve ambiguous identifiers and ensure that physical choices preserve business semantics.

ambition.what: No broader service or decision right is assumed.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: database modelling tools can export dialect-specific descriptions from explicitly declared types, identifiers, keys and relationships.

assumptions: Boundary covers the architect's own writing and coding route allowed by the task, not directing another coder or deploying definitions. If coding is delegated instead, ownership and other-role effort must be measured separately.

The design owner supplies the approved model and target dialect; database owners supply namespace conventions. s1 checks gaps and s2 counts all missing logical and physical specification, including exact object ids, types, keys and constraints.
OTHER means the database modelling tool. Native export first; unsupported features are manually coded within retained s3 time. No language model is needed for a declared model-to-code translation.

Shares and reductions are provisional scenarios, not measured baselines. Same-system saving stays fully retained and earns no saving. Overlap with application database design and architecture documentation must be reconciled before roll-up.
research_questions: Does generated code preserve a reviewed model's identifiers and constraints exactly?
Which constructs still require hand coding?

already_counted.description: Check native export and manually handle unsupported constructs

incremental.description: Maintain target dialect and namespace export settings

approvals.approved_version: approved database description code v1; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross 22.25 minus 1 upkeep gives 21.25. High allows 4.25 more hours of unsupported dialect coding; low applies when exports already exist or the model cannot drive them.

role.altitude: The architect can spend less time assembling code and comparison tables while retaining diagnosis, design meaning and approval of each bounded change.
reach: Prepare reproducible regression evidence with quality analysts after learning fixture and assertion design.
Frame technical evaluation criteria with procurement before a technology purchase.
skills_to_grow: Distinguish static compliance from semantic correctness
Maintain explicit model and dialect contracts
role.ambitious_version: Produce a traceable technical recommendation or verified correction whose assumptions and evidence can be inspected by the next decision owner.
